channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Turn Claude Code into a plugin-powered teammate: a hands-on guide to Anthropic's official plugin directory
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic's official Claude Code plugin directory (anthropics/claude-plugins-official, 42K+ stars, Apache-2.0) bundles 40 internal plugins and 14 community plugins installable with one /plugin command. Hands-on: code-review, frontend-design, and the Playwright MCP plugin, plus what to know before you trust a plugin.

item.title: vLLM 0.32.0 is out: ask models questions, get probabilities — and your server stops trusting every website
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: vLLM shipped version 0.32.0 today with a structured-decisions endpoint that answers yes/no, choice, and score questions with calibrated probabilities instead of generated text, plus 814 commits of KV-cache speedups, Model Runner V2, and a long-overdue CORS lockdown.

item.title: Give Blender an AI copilot: hands-on with mcp-for-blender-pro
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A hands-on guide to anujasid/blender-ai-mcp-addon: install the add-on in Blender 4.2+, connect Claude, GPT, Gemini or a local Ollama model, and direct your 3D scenes in plain English — with 21 scene tools and a built-in MCP server for coding agents.

item.title: Teach your agent any website: turn web pages into callable APIs with api-anything
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A hands-on guide to goodnight000/api-anything: install the CLI, run a bundled operation, plug it into your coding agent over MCP, then teach it a site of your own — no browser driving required.

item.title: OpenCode confirms breach: a 'large scale distillation attack' stole provider API keys from 1.4% of Console users
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenCode disclosed on October 17, 2026 that a "large scale distillation attack" breached a legacy system, possibly exposing the OpenAI, Anthropic and Google API keys saved in 1.4% of Console users' workspaces — and told victims to revoke their keys now.

item.title: Anthropic’s Jack Clark tells the IMF and World Bank AI could push US GDP to $44T by 2030 — and wants ‘unusual and serious rules’
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark told finance ministers and central bankers in Bangkok that one of the lab’s internal economic models forecasts US GDP reaching about $44 trillion by 2030 — and called for international cooperation on ‘unusual and serious rules’ for AI.

item.title: Give your AI app a tactile glass interface: a hands-on guide to Solid Glass
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Solid Glass (deeplethe/solid-glass, MIT, ~1,700 stars in its first week) is a glass-inspired design system for AI apps built on shadcn/ui: one stylesheet plus a registry of agent-oriented components — status lines, tool steps, diff views — installable with two npx commands. Here is how to put it in your app.

item.title: Sparkian launches a $19 AI workspace: 100+ models in one chat
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Geekflare's Sparkian launches a $19/month Pro plan with 100+ models in one chat, side-by-side answers, and 10,000 Sparks covering chat and image generation.

item.title: Give your coding agent ears: a hands-on guide to earshot
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: earshot (Leonxlnx/earshot, MIT, past 500 GitHub stars) gives coding agents ears: describe, match, find and critique audio from the CLI, forge sounds as code, and fit recordings into editable code. CPU-only, offline after a 1.4 GB download.

item.title: DeepSeek ships V4.1-Flash-1017: 77.0 on DeepSWE, MIT weights, and a $0.75 Search API
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017 on October 17, 2026: a minor update that scores 77.0 on DeepSWE v1.1, ahead of Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol, with MIT-licensed weights, unchanged $0.15/$0.60 per-million-token pricing, and a newly opened Search API at $0.75 per 1,000 calls.

item.title: Query your codebase instead of grepping it: a hands-on guide to Graphify
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Graphify (Graphify-Labs/graphify, Apache-2.0, past 127,000 GitHub stars) turns your code, docs, SQL schemas, and PDFs into a knowledge graph your AI assistant can query — parsed locally with tree-sitter, no LLM, nothing leaves your machine. This guide installs it, builds your first graph, wires it into your coding assistant, and keeps it fresh.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz and NVIDIA lock in a decade of AI driving: one stack from MB.OS to robolimousines
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Announced October 16, the expanded partnership fuses Mercedes-Benz engineering and MB.OS with NVIDIA's Hyperion compute architecture, Alpamayo AI reasoning stack, and Halos safety system — targeting future SAE Level 4 driving, including robolimousines.

item.title: Rebuild any app and fix what its users hate: a hands-on guide to the Replica skill set
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Replica (Jakeschincariol/replica-skill, MIT, roughly 2,900 GitHub stars in its first two weeks) is eleven free Claude skills that reverse-engineer any app, rebuild it clean-room style, test it, and turn its users' complaints into your launch angle. This hands-on guide walks the full pipeline, tool by tool.

item.title: China moves to fence in AI: 23 AI technologies proposed for export controls, registration starts today
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: On October 16, China's commerce and science ministries proposed adding 40 technologies — 23 of them AI — to the export-control catalogue, and imposed an immediate pre-export registration requirement. Open-source and API services get carve-outs; public comments are open until November 15.

item.title: Beam's weights are out: Reflection ships its 501B open-weight model under Apache 2.0
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Reflection AI released the weights for Beam, its first open-weight model, on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 license — with BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 checkpoints, post-training recipes, a safety technical report, and day-0 support from more than 40 launch partners.

item.title: Chery's AiMOGA opens global pre-orders for Mobo, a 22-DOF home-companion humanoid
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AiMOGA Robotics, Chery's robotics brand, will open global pre-orders for Mobo — its first consumer humanoid robot built for home companionship — at the Chery International User Summit in Wuhu, October 19–23.

item.title: Kling 4.0 goes global: 30-second AI video, 15 reference assets, and a pitch at the pros
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Kling AI's new video generation model doubles single-clip length to 30 seconds and adds keyframe-level control, aiming to move AI video from viral clips to professional production.

item.title: From whisky to wattage: Taiwan's Agencia Comercial Spirits signs up to $400M for AI compute in Indonesia
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Nasdaq-listed Agencia Comercial Spirits — a premium whisky company — committed up to $400M over five years for AI computing capacity in Indonesia. The catch: the payments don't depend on customers ever showing up.

item.title: Li Auto bets RMB1.625B on its own silicon: Mahe Xin's 1280-TOPS M100 chip gets a funding round
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Li Auto is putting RMB1.625 billion (~$224M) into its chip and domain controller business: Shanghai Mahe Xin Technology will issue new equity, Li Auto takes RMB1.0B of it, outside investors RMB625M, and Li Auto keeps a 74.01% controlling stake. The money backs the 5nm, 1280-TOPS Mahe M100 automotive AI chip that went into mass production in May.

item.title: Turn your JavaScript into a neural net — no training required: a hands-on guide to Handwired
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Handwired (MIT, about 1,500 GitHub stars in its first two days) turns ordinary JavaScript — if-else, loops, state — into an exact, differentiable numeric program built from matrix multiplies and ReLU gates. This hands-on guide clones the repo, runs the demos, walks the toggle-switch template, and wires your first program.

item.title: Algosoup launches algofin 1.0: a finance decision model banks can run air-gapped on one GPU
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: London's Algosoup has launched algofin 1.0, an AI model trained for financial decisions that banks and financial firms can license and run inside their own networks — including air-gapped, on a single GPU. It scores 84.8 on financial sentiment, 79.4 on banking intent and 93.6 on scam detection, all zero-shot.

item.title: Open Source AI Week kicks off: 65 events over 10 days as the Bay Area bets on open AI
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A new nonprofit, the Open Intelligence Foundation, is stewarding a 10-day, community-run Open Source AI Week in the San Francisco Bay Area: more than 60 events from October 16 to 25, anchored by a Hugging Face kickoff party, an ExecuTorch hackathon, and a debate on open versus closed AI models.

item.title: RapidCanvas raises $29M Series B: Vertex Ventures bets on 'managed AI execution' as ARR grows 8x in six quarters
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: RapidCanvas has raised $29 million in Series B funding led by Vertex Ventures SEA & India to scale its 'managed AI execution' model for mid-size enterprises — pairing an agentic AI platform with field engineers who stay accountable for production outcomes.

item.title: RTX Spark laptops hit shelves worldwide: NVIDIA’s 128GB local-AI machines start at $2,599
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA announced on October 16, 2026 that RTX Spark laptops are available globally from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI, starting at $2,599 — a Grace-Blackwell superchip with up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of FP4 compute, built for running AI agents on the device.

item.title: Run a 321B AI model on your own GPU: a hands-on guide to Project Maya
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Project Maya (mw00/project-maya, MIT, about 900 GitHub stars in its first ten days) runs Z.ai's 321-billion-parameter GLM-5.3-Flash on your own GPUs — one card up to sixteen — tiering model experts across GPU, RAM, and NVMe SSD, served through an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API. This hands-on guide installs it, picks the right quant for your memory pool, and wires it into your tools.
